payload.prfaq:
PRESS RELEASE. quackitect's gates now review themselves. Every gate carries four rounds it cannot skip - verify what each input state actually delivered, validate the work against the requirement REGISTER rather than its own plan, argue the opposing case with a named kill-criterion, and reach a verdict that can be REOPEN. Reopen now does something: it re-activates the named states and everything derived from them, marking the first pass superseded rather than deleting it, so a reader sees what was claimed and that it did not survive. Underneath, the lane stops being the slow way to work: ripgrep for the tree, git for the record, reads in parts, edits in batches, and a config lane for the settings nobody could reach.

HOSTILE FAQ.

Q: You added four mandatory fields to every gate. Is this not just more paperwork?
A: It would be, if the rounds were decoration. The test is whether they CHANGE anything. This rewalk's own rounds already reversed an architecture decision, corrected a requirement's pass line so it cannot be satisfied by redefinition, and found an unimplemented verdict. If a future retro finds that no redteam_round ever changed a conclusion, the round has become ceremony and needs an adversarial party rather than more prose - that tripwire is logged.

Q: The same agent writes the decision AND the red-team against it. Is that not theatre by construction?
A: It is weaker than v1's answer, which was a human adjudicator, and I am not going to claim otherwise. What makes it more than theatre is the KILL-CRITERION: naming what would have to be true for this to be the wrong call is a falsifiable act, and then you either find it or you do not. What it cannot do is make me want to find it. The structural fix is a separate reviewing party and it is explicitly out of scope.

Q: You reopened 30 fills across 46 states. How is that not just deleting a day's work?
A: Nothing was deleted. The fills are marked superseded, the evidence files are on disk, the history keeps every entry. The cost is re-walking, which is exactly what the owner asked for, and the record is now MORE informative than a clean first pass would have been: it shows a decision, a review, and a reversal.

Q: Three mechanisms were 'written but never collected'. What makes you think you found all of them?
A: Nothing does, and I am not claiming it. Three were found in one day by accident - the scan, the guidance join, the review rounds - which suggests the method notes should be swept SYSTEMATICALLY against the evidence forms rather than waiting for the next accident. That sweep is not in this iteration's scope and it should be somebody's.

Q: The rounds are required now. What stops an agent writing 'looks fine' four times?
A: The form cannot stop it. The kill-criterion rule makes it visible - a round with no criterion named is not a round - and a retro can count rounds that changed nothing. That is honest enforcement rather than strong enforcement, and the difference is recorded.

Q: You changed the architecture after the architecture gate was blessed. Does that not make the gate meaningless?
A: The opposite - it makes it mean something for the first time. The first blessing had no verify round, so nothing read the register against the design and the R3 violation passed. The reopen path exists precisely so a gate can be wrong and be corrected without pretending it was right.

Q: What is the single thing most likely to be wrong here?
A: That I am the one judging whether my own red-team was adversarial enough. Everything else in this iteration is checkable by something other than me.
payload.findings_folded:
TWO THINGS CHANGED UPSTREAM, and one question could not be answered cleanly and became a recorded gap rather than a scope item.

1. THE SWEEP QUESTION IS NEW AND UNANSWERED. 'What makes you think you found all of them?' has no good answer: three written-but-never-collected mechanisms were found by ACCIDENT in one day. That implies a systematic sweep of every method note against the evidence forms that should collect it. It is not in scope, it is bigger than a note, and inventing it here would widen the iteration - so it goes to the register as owed work rather than into the plan.

2. THE HONEST CEILING OF THE RED-TEAM IS NOW STATED IN THE PRESS RELEASE ITSELF rather than only in RAID: the same agent writes the decision and the case against it, the kill-criterion is what keeps that from being circular, and the structural answer is a separate party that is deliberately not built. Putting it in the FAQ means a reader meets the limitation at the same time as the feature.

NOT FOLDED, deliberately: the 'more paperwork' objection needed no upstream change - it is answered by whether the rounds change anything, and this rewalk is the first datum. And the reopen-deletes-work objection was already answered by the design, which is why supersede-not-erase was chosen before anyone asked.
